articleTitle: Research on Rotor Side Controller of Doubly-fed Machine Based on Multi-layer Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Control (RAIIC)
abstract: With the proposal of “carbon peak and carbon neutrality” goals, the decreasing of coal resources,the environmental problems caused by conventional thermal power generation, the new energy power generation including wind is increasing. The special advantages of Doubly-fed Machine (DFM) make it a good choice for wind power generation, and the research of improving its performance became a hotspot. At present, PI controller is widely used to drive DFM in industry, but this control strategy relies on accurate mathematical model parameters, and when the motor model parameters are inaccurate, the control performance will decline, reducing the dependence of control strategy on model parameters is a problem worth studying, This paper proposes a rotor side controller based on multi-layer neural network in response to the complexity of DFM control system, analyses its designing process and giving the simulation results. Compared with PI control strategy, the multi-layer neural network controller designed in this paper can better adapt to the change of motor running state, dynamic response speed is faster, and the overall robustness is better.

articleTitle: Modified flocking model for autonomous vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Control (RAIIC)
abstract: A modified flocking model for autonomous aircraft is proposed. Influence for mode of trajectory of collective motion by some restriction to flock’s objects flight velocity are considered. Assumes that there is no control from a single center, but only by the using of information about the location of neighboring flying vehicles and flight velocity restriction allow us to arrange desired flock’s collective movement. The considered approach uses numerical simulation of the flight of each individual device based on the translational and rotational equations of the quadcopter in Earth coordinate system.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Fault Diagnosis of Rolling Bearings Based on MS-CNN and BiLSTM-Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Control (RAIIC)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that it is difficult to diagnose rolling bearings under variable speed and small sample scenarios, a comprehensive fault diagnosis model of rolling bearings based on improved deep network was proposed. First of all, By combining multi-scale convolutional neural network (MSCNN) and bi-directional long short-term memory (BI-LSTM), multiscale convolutional neural network (MSCNN) and bi-directional long short-term memory BILSTM) network to form a parallel MSCNN-BILSTM network, and the two network channels were used to obtain the multi-scale feature information and time feature information of the vibration signal respectively. Secondly, feature fusion was performed in the aggregation layer. Then, the attention mechanism module was introduced to perform feature selection on the output of the convergence layer through the weighting layer. Finally, the trained MS-CNN and BiLSTM-Attention model and other classical models were applied to the measured rolling bearing data set for experimental comparison in two scenarios of variable speed combined with small sample size. The analysis shows that the average accuracy of the proposed model in the variable speed scenario is $99.72 \%$, which is higher than other models. The experimental results also show that the proposed model has higher recognition accuracy and better robustness.

articleTitle: 3D Path Planning Digital Twins for Robot Arms Incorporating Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Control (RAIIC)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of low motion efficiency of the robotic arm in the space full of obstacles and the inability to monitor the operation status in real time, this paper firstly designs the digital twin system architecture to realize the virtual reality mapping and interaction. Secondly, considering the requirement of robotic arm path planning, a digital twin-based APF-SAC path planning method is proposed, which optimizes the path generated by the artificial potential field method as the reference path and incorporates it into the reward function to accelerate the convergence speed of the traditional SAC algorithm, and introduces the recent experience playback technology to improve the stability and speed of training. Experiments based on the proposed algorithm show that the path imitation mechanism can improve the training efficiency, and the APF-SAC algorithm can plan the path more reasonably compared with the PPO algorithm. On this basis, the digital twin system is used to realize the real-time preview of the algorithm, which ensures the availability of the path and the safety of the robotic arm.

articleTitle: Augmented Reality-Based Robot Interaction and Modeling System: An Innovative Human-Machine Interaction Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Control (RAIIC)
abstract: Traditional robot modeling approaches often lack intuitiveness and efficiency. To facilitate more convenient and intuitive complex robot design and modeling, this paper aims to design and implement an augmented reality-based robot interaction and modeling system. This system enables modeling and controlling robots using Meta Quest 3 controllers, and achieves interactive effects between virtual robots and the real environment through the headset. By integrating key technologies such as robot control algorithms, augmented reality rendering techniques, and physics engines, the system can precisely control robots and merge virtual content with the real environment. User study results indicate that the system effectively achieves humanoid robot control and modeling.

articleTitle: Visibility enhancement of sand-dust images based on depthwise separable convolution
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Control (RAIIC)
abstract: To address the visual interference problem in “sand-blind” environments, where sand images suffer from color shifts and severe loss of background detail, we propose a sand image enhancement algorithm based on color correction and depthwise separable convolution. First, the color correction module preprocesses the synthetic sand images to correct color deviations. Then, the SMU (Separable Multi-scale Unit) is applied within the decoupling reconstruction module to address gradient vanishing and extract degradation information. Finally, aggregated depthwise separable convolutions are added to the denoising module to learn textures, thereby obtaining more effective information and target features. Experiments on synthetic datasets demonstrate that, compared to mainstream algorithms such as TFIO, GDCP, AWC, and HRDCP, our algorithm achieves at least 10.46% and 35.56% improvements in PSNR and SSIM metrics, respectively, better restoring image details obscured by sand.

articleTitle: Research on Denoising Technology for Yimeng Red Films Based on Swin Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Control (RAIIC)
abstract: This research introduces a novel method for denoising Yimeng red films by integrating Swin Transformer and Generative Adversarial Network (GAN). The Swin Transformer effectively extracts both local and global features of video frames through its hierarchical structure and window attention mechanism. Meanwhile, the GAN enhances the realism and detail preservation of the denoised videos through adversarial training. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves a PSNR value of 36.47 and an SSIM value of 0.940 in the YOUKUVESR dataset, outperforming other advanced algorithms. This provides a new solution for old film restoration and contributes to the preservation of cultural heritage.

articleTitle: A Pedestrian Detection Network Based on EfficientDet Combined with SCConv
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Control (RAIIC)
abstract: Addressing the common issues of false detections and missed detections in pedestrian detection tasks, especially when dealing with multi-scale targets and occlusions, we propose a single-stage target detection network architecture based on EfficientDet, named PSC-EfficientDet-D0. This architecture aims to enhance detection speed and model efficiency while ensuring accuracy. Specifically, we first restructure the inverted residual bottleneck network to improve the backbone network EfficientNet, which boosts accuracy while maintaining relatively low parameter counts and frame rates. Additionally, we introduce NWD Loss to further enhance the model’s capability to detect targets of varying scales and improve target localization. Experimental results show that our improved method has achieved significant performance enhancements, especially in the detection of tiny targets. Rather than EfficientNet-D0, our PSC-EfficientNet-D0 has demonstrated $2.1 \%$ increase in accuracy and $A P_{50: 95}^{{small }}$ on the Pascal VOC 2007 dataset. For pedestrian detection tasks, there has been a $1.1 \%$ improvement in average precision (AP). The enhanced EfficientDet exhibits stronger robustness and generalization capabilities.

articleTitle: Unity 3D-Based Six-Degree-of-Freedom Robotic Arm Virtual Simulation Teaching Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Control (RAIIC)
abstract: The robotic arm is an important foundation for robots to perform a variety of complex tasks, and the robotic arm grasping technology involves multidisciplinary and multidisciplinary fields, which leads to a high learning threshold due to reasons such as more complex and abstract theoretical knowledge. In addition, the whole set of industrial robots is expensive, and it is difficult to ensure that each experimenter is involved. To address these issues, this paper is based on the visualization of Unity3D development platform vision technology, using SolidWorks modeling, and combined with the actual scene in the robotic arm grasping operations, to achieve a highly immersive virtual simulation of a typical case of grasping the target object, to build a six-degree-of-freedom robotic arm virtual simulation teaching system; to achieve the virtual simulation teaching software and the robotic arm unit to establish communication, the The virtual simulation system is integrated with the robotic arm unit operation platform. The system has the advantages of easy operation, real simulation effect and good learning effect, which is of positive significance for improving the teaching quality and research level of robot arm related courses.

articleTitle: Improved beluga self-resistant welding depth of fusion control based on Smith predictor
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Control (RAIIC)
abstract: Aiming at the many parameters of the self-immunity controller, the strong hysteresis and large inertia of the laser welding system, a transfer function model is established according to the control system characteristics of the welding system, and the instability elements of the model are analyzed. A self-immobilizing controller based on Smith predictor is designed, combined with the improved beluga algorithm. Experimental simulation of the model is carried out by modeling the effect of disturbances on the system using unit step response curves. The results show that the tracking speed is fast and stable tracking within 2.2s, with better disturbance suppression ability and higher control accuracy when using the optimized self-anti-jamming controller based on Smith’s improved Moby Dick optimization for controlling the welding melt depth system.

articleTitle: Color image encryption based on improved Henon hyperchaotic mapping
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Control (RAIIC)
abstract: About the problems of all little blank, let droop complexity and small lyapunov index of two-dimensional Henon chaotic mapping. In this one article, an better Henon chaotic map is proposed, which adopts the classical scrambling diffusion structure. A replacement algorithm is designed to replace image pixels into different rows and columns, and a non-sequential diffusion algorithm is also designed. The performance simulation results show that the proposed encryption algorithm has large key space, high key sensitivity, uniform distribution of ciphertext statistical histogram, low correlation between adjacent pixels, information entropy close to the ideal value, strong anti-differential cryptanalysis ability and high security.

articleTitle: Real-time monitoring of trucks used in open pit based on aerial video of UAV
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Control (RAIIC)
abstract: In recent years, accidents in open-pit coal mines have occurred frequently, followed by safety production and emergency rescue issues. The drone has the advantages of flexible perspective, wide field of view, and convenient scene switching. The use of drones to realize the monitoring of the freight system of surface coal mines can reduce the cost of manpower, ensure production safety, and improve the level of intelligence. More importantly, standardized drone monitoring can determine the rescue location at the first time after the accident. However, it is not enough to use UAV just for data acquisition. It is important to obtain the location of trucks and workers quickly, in real time, and accurately in complex environments. A system on module chip was installed on the UAV to perform real-time computation, and the improved YOLOv7-tiny target detection model was deployed for real-time target detection in this paper. The detection performance of the proposed method was compared against five conventional detection methods. The results demonstrate that the proposed detection approach outperforms other conventional detection approaches in all datasets selected for experiments. Especially, the proposed method maintained mAP of above $89 \%$ in object-level detection for open pit datasets. The performance of truck real-time detection from open-pit coal mine images has been significantly improved. This research will contribute to the safety of the entire production process.

articleTitle: Research on SF6 Leakage Detection Based on Artificial Intelligence Gas Cloud Leakage Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Control (RAIIC)
abstract: Sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) gas is extensively used in high-voltage equipment such as transformers and circuit breakers due to its excellent insulation and arc-extinguishing properties. However, SF6 gas leakage poses significant safety and environmental risks. This study aims to develop an AI-based gas cloud leakage detection algorithm that utilizes infrared imaging data and deep neural networks for real-time detection and localization of SF6 gas leaks. The proposed method integrates infrared imaging technology with advanced deep learning algorithms to enhance detection accuracy and sensitivity, reducing the need for manual intervention. Experimental results show that the system achieves an overall detection accuracy of $82.71 \%$, with a missed detection rate of $\mathbf{1 3. 8 8 \%}$ and a false alarm rate of $3.41 \%$. This approach ensures the safety of equipment and personnel, and mitigates environmental impact, providing a reliable and efficient solution for SF6 leakage detection in the power industry.

articleTitle: Optimized HMI Strategies for Collaborative Driving Interfaces in L3+ Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Control (RAIIC)
abstract: Amidst the pivotal transition of autonomous vehicles from Level 2 to Level 3, a fundamental paradigm shift occurs, moving from a shared human-machine control framework to a complete transfer of driving responsibilities. In this evolving context, the automated system assumes a primary role in executing driving tasks, while the driver transitions to a supervisory role, overseeing system behavior and intervening only when deemed necessary. This transition necessitates addressing complex challenges encompassing safety, liability, workload distribution, alongside fostering human-machine trust and enhancing system interpretability. To address these multifaceted challenges, we introduce a comprehensive human-machine shared driving interaction design strategy, referred to as the TSE design method. This strategy encapsulates the entire driving journey, commencing with pre-journey training and preparation, encompassing safe driving practices during the journey, and culminating in post-journey performance evaluation. Our primary emphasis lies in the intricate analysis of human-machine safety interaction strategies during the actual driving phase. Based on the current system status and road conditions, the automated system dynamically apportions driving tasks to the driver, considering factors such as the driver’s workload, engagement level, and the complexity of take-over tasks. Furthermore, we delve into the intersectional impact of various factors, including the driver’s mental model, attention allocation, situational awareness, human-machine trust, system transparency, and interpretive interfaces, on the overall performance of the human-machine shared driving system. To demonstrate the practical application of our design principles, we present concrete design exemplars derived from driver training sessions and take-over interaction design. These instances illustrate the effectiveness of our TSE design method in enhancing the safety, trust, and interpretability of the human-machine shared driving system. This paper presents a comprehensive and systematic methodology for the design of L3+ autonomous driving human-machine interactions, thereby offering profound insights and cutting-edge solutions to automotive manufacturers in their pursuit of optimizing human-machine interaction design endeavors.

articleTitle: Research on Regional Dual Carbon Goals and Path Planning Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Control (RAIIC)
abstract: The research focuses on achieving regional dual carbon targets in China by enhancing energy efficiency and increasing the use of non-fossil fuels, tailored to China’s specific policy and economic needs. Various mathematical models were employed to analyze the dynamic relationships between carbon emissions, economic growth, and energy consumption. The research developed multiple scenario analysis models, including a carbon emission model based on the Markov decision process and an energy consumption forecast model influenced by demographic and economic changes. The findings demonstrate that comprehensive measures to improve energy efficiency, upgrade industrial technology, and decarbonize energy sources effectively advance the achievement of regional dual carbon goals.

articleTitle: Multi-Target Tracking Method for Drone Swarm Based on Interaction Feature Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Control (RAIIC)
abstract: This paper proposes a Multi-Target Tracking Method for Drone Swarm Based on Interaction Feature Extraction. These challenges include sparse and homogenized appearance features among individuals, mutual occlusion of individuals within the cluster, and platform shaking. The algorithm first introduces a self-attentive feature mask to enhance the effect of graph convolutional neural network (GCN) on trajectory aggregation. Secondly, IOU and possibility-based C -mean clustering are combined to improve the extraction of motion features and differentiate neighboring targets within clusters. Finally, the tracking results are further optimized using a Graph Attention Convolutional Network (GAT) and Gaussian smoothing interpolation algorithm. The algorithm proposed utilises short-time trajectory aggregation and long-time trajectory matching to achieve multi-target tracking of infrared Drone swarm. The algorithm only utilises motion and interaction information. Experiments were conducted on the infrared Drone swarm multi-target tracking dataset. The tracking method presented in this paper was compared with other advanced tracking algorithms and exhibited higher performance metrics. Specifically, MOTA and IDF1 reached $84.9 \%$ and $80.2 \%$, respectively. The method also demonstrated superior tracking results in complex scenarios, such as targets occluding each other and platform swaying.

articleTitle: Radioactive Source Detection System Based on Autonomous Mobile Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Control (RAIIC)
abstract: The intensive application of radioactive sources in various fields has led to a rise in incidents involving their loss. Focusing on the rapid and safe detection of radiation environments and the localization of radioactive sources, this paper integrates the design of detection robots, radiation localization techniques, and path tracking to create a radioactive source detection system based on autonomous mobile robots. The design of the detection robot considers the unique challenges posed by radiation environments. In terms of localization, an adaptive radioactive source localization algorithm based on the Bayesian model, incorporating angle of arrival (AOA), is proposed to estimate the location of radioactive sources. Path planning is optimized using the Pure Pursuit algorithm to enhance tracking accuracy. Finally, on a mobile robot platform, an unknown radioactive source search experiment is conducted, validating the effectiveness of the system and vigorously advancing the field of radioactive source detection.

articleTitle: Integrating U-net and Multi-Model Approaches for Accurate Dental Occlusal Surface and Caries Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Control (RAIIC)
abstract: Dental caries, a widespread oral health issue, results in significant morbidity and high treatment costs globally. Traditional detection methods often miss early-stage lesions, necessitating advanced diagnostic techniques. This study integrates machine vision and deep learning to enhance caries detection. Using a U-Net network with an attention mechanism, we establish maxillofacial morphological standards, achieving precise dental recognition and classification. Our method segments dental images and detects caries lesions with a chalky algorithm based on HSV color space. Experimental results show significant improvements in recognition accuracy, F1-score, and AUC over traditional methods. Models based on molar occlusal contours and fissure patterns are trained with attention-enhanced U-net networks, then combined using weighted averaging for model fusion. This multi-model fusion approach yields a recognition accuracy of 0.7792, an F1-score of 0.9061, and an AUC of 0.9026, marking improvements of 15.78% in accuracy, 10.57% in AUC, and 7.01% in F1-score over the original U-Net network. Our method simplifies traditional dental examination procedures, enabling flexible and precise caries detection in home intelligent medical settings, thereby reducing the incidence of dental caries.

articleTitle: A Convolutional Heterogeneous Spiking Neural Network for Real-time Music Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Control (RAIIC)
abstract: While artificial Neural Networks(ANNs) have gradually become the dominating frameworks for music classification, single-structured ANNs have certain functional and computational limitations to meet real-time and low-latency requirement in this era of the Internet of Things. With Convolutional Neural Network(CNN) module to address spatial correlations and Recurrent Neural Networks(RNN) module to capture temporal dependencies, hybrid CNN-RNN architectures have attracted academic focus. However, the inference promptness and energy efficiency of these hybrid models are still confined by their computationally costly RNN modules. With sparse and binary activated data flows, the brain-inspired Spiking Neural Networks(SNNs) enable RNN-like sequential processing in a computationally efficient and economic way. Taking respective advantages of dynamically different spiking neurons, we proposed the Convolutional Heterogeneous Spiking Neural Network(CHSNN). With deliberate choices of input spectrograms and training strategy, the proposed CHSNN have outperformed most existing CNN-RNN classification models, demonstrated satisfactory real-time processing ability even with only 20.8% inference time steps, and shown the substitutability of SNN against RNN in terms of both classification performance and inference latency.

articleTitle: J1F Tracking: Online Multi-Camera People Tracking In Just 1 Frame
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Control (RAIIC)
abstract: Multi-Camera People Tracking (MCPT) has become an increasingly important research field and has achieved rapid development, but there are still problems such as occlusion, ID change, and tracking loss. So far, most algorithms are offline algorithms that use the information of past frames and future frames to match and track using the re-identification method. We propose an online tracking algorithm that can online tracking using just the past 1 frame (named J1F). This method uses the position and appearance features of the target person to perform collaborative analysis between multiple cameras, and uses the majority camera voting method to track the same target person in the current frame. Improve the efficiency of Multi-Camera People Tracking by using a more efficient and robust method. The method was evaluated on the AI City 2024 dataset, and the HOTA reached $70.15 \%$, reducing the time consumption by $31.7 \%$.

articleTitle: Autonomous Terrain-Aided Navigation System based on Non-Rigid MBES Digital Twin
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Control (RAIIC)
abstract: This paper introduces an Autonomous TerrainAided Navigation (TAN) system leveraging Non-Rigid Multibeam Echo Sounder (MBES) Digital Twin technology, termed DT-NR-PF. The system simulates the measurement behavior of MBES sensors underwater and predicts measurements, thereby reducing the parameter count essential for the MBES digital twin model construction. By integrating multivariate linear regression with non-rigid MBES digital twin models, it independently estimates the velocity of Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs), eliminating the reliance on external reference navigation systems. This advancement enhances the capability and autonomy of MBES as a standalone navigation device. Experimental outcomes demonstrate the system’s proficiency in executing TAN without the need for Sound Velocity Profile data or external velocity measurement devices, thus facilitating the development of the autonomous TAN system.

articleTitle: Optimization of Visual SLAM for Mobile Robots in Complex Environments: Tight Coupling of Visual-Inertial Fusion and Efficient Loop Closure Detection Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Control (RAIIC)
abstract: This study tackles mobile robots’ environmental perception challenges in complexity, presenting an advanced Visual-Inertial SLAM (VSLAM) technique that enhances accuracy, robustness, and real-time functionality. It bolsters visual odometry with ORB features for meticulous matching and selects keyframes, integrating IMU data for robust motion handling in low-textured scenes. Rear-end operations employ graph optimization and a bag-of-words-based loop closure, utilizing sliding window optimization and marginalization to curb accumulative errors, ensuring trajectory and map consistency. Experiments on KITTI, EuRoC, and TUM datasets surpass conventional methods like ORB-SLAM2 and VINS-Mono, trimming trajectory and mapping inaccuracies by 23.8% and 4.1%, respectively, with robust adaptability across motion modes and environments. System module timing analysis paves the way for real-time deployment on less powerful hardware. Future research directions include direct visual odometry, dynamic environment adaptation, multi-sensor fusion, and largescale scene comprehension, pushing SLAM’s frontier in intricate dynamics and empowering autonomous robot navigation.

articleTitle: Wearable pressure sensors for muscle movement detection with high sensitivity and accuracy
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Control (RAIIC)
abstract: Human motion recognition, known for its high accuracy and rapid response, has long been considered a crucial component in human-computer interaction activities such as rehabilitation robots, medical prostheses, and wearable electronic devices. To develop an efficient and reliable motion intention recognition system, the force myography (FMG) technique, which detects muscle surface pressure signals, has been a primary focus of research. However, current FMG technology has limitations in intention recognition accuracy, individual adaptability, and closed-loop control precision. To address these shortcomings, this study proposes an FMG human motion sensing strategy based on a flexible piezoresistive material sensor. Leveraging the ultra-high sensitivity (up to $0.712 \mathrm{~N}^{-1}$) and low activation pressure (less than 0.05 N) of this pressure sensor, FMG signals can be accurately acquired from sensors strapped to the forearm. The results demonstrate that this sensor offers higher sensitivity under the same external force compared to traditional sandwich sensing structures. The application of this highly sensitive pressure sensor in wearable systems provides a valuable tool for detecting minute human pressure signals and holds significant potential in the fields of rehabilitation and medicine.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Bionic Specialized Cargo Quadrupedal UAV
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Control (RAIIC)
abstract: With the rapid advancements in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) technology, new solutions have emerged to address logistics challenges in certain areas. Drone deliveries can reach locations that are inaccessible to traditional logistics methods. However, existing cargo drones face difficulties with takeoff and landing on complex terrains due to their fixed landing gear. This paper introduces the design of a bionic specialized quadrupedal UAV, capable of moving and climbing on complex terrains, aimed at improving UAV cargo operations in challenging environments.

articleTitle: Review of Cable-driven Hyper-redundant Robotic Arms
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Control (RAIIC)
abstract: Cable-driven hyper-redundant robotic arms (CHRA) are robotic arms with redundant degrees of freedom (DOF), inspired by snake-like biomimicry principles, utilizing cables as the driving mechanism. Compared to traditional rigid robotic arms, CHRA showcase unparalleled advantages in complex and confined application scenarios such as aerospace engines, aircraft fuel tanks, space stations, and nuclear power plant pipelines. Furthermore, they boast a wide range of potential applications and currently stand as a prominent research topic in the field of robotics. This paper provides a comprehensive review of CHRA in recent years, analyzing and summarizing the technologies and scientific issues associated with these arms from four perspectives: driving methods, modeling approaches, trajectory planning, and control. We conclude by summarizing the challenges currently faced by CHRA, providing insights into their future prospects, and shedding light on their evolving trends in the field of robotics.

articleTitle: Intelligent Security Q&A System Based on Large Language Model
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Control (RAIIC)
abstract: With the continuous development of artificial intelligence technology, intelligent Q&A systems have been widely used in various fields, including hotels, airports, hospitals and other places. However, traditional Q&A systems are often constrained by the limited rule base and stereotypical dialog flow, and are unable to provide a sufficiently intelligent interaction experience. The system in this paper utilizes Large Language Model (LLM) combined with face recognition technology to build a more intelligent and flexible security Q&A system. By combining the local knowledge base with LLM, the system is able to retrieve relevant information from the local knowledge base based on the professional questions provided by the user through text vectorization and then similarity comparison, and generate corresponding responses, thus providing a more humanized and accurate service. The system has the following capabilities: (1) specialized Q&A, based on LLM and self-constructed knowledge base to generate Q&A with domain-specific knowledge, compared to model fine-tuning methods, this method can deploy large vertical domain models without re-training;(2) Security welcome, this system face recognition module adopts Python+Dlib method to identify the user and conduct the welcome greeting, if the visitor is an unfamiliar user, it is not possible to conduct the Q&A with the LLM for the sensitive information, e.g., private information, etc.; if the visitor is a known user, then it is possible to communicate with the LLM in all aspects.

articleTitle: Dynamic Weighted Multidimensional Similarity Matrix Data Grafting Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Control (RAIIC)
abstract: Data source matching and missing value imputation are crucial challenges in the integration of multisource heterogeneous data in the era of big data. This paper proposes a novel data grafting algorithm based on dynamic weighted similarity matrices. The algorithm constructs dynamic weight similarity matrices that capture the complex relationships between multidimensional features, optimizes similarity function parameters, and comprehensively integrates feature similarities to guide the selection of the most similar samples for data source matching and precise imputation of missing values. Experimental results on a dataset of Chinese city statistics demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms traditional approaches such as mean imputation and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) in terms of Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), validating the effectiveness and superiority of the algorithm. The dynamic weighted similarity matrix model presented in this paper provides a new perspective for high-quality fusion of multi-source heterogeneous data.

articleTitle: TDOA based Tightly Coupled Sensor Fusion for UAV Positioning in GPS-denied Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Control (RAIIC)
abstract: Currently, the integration of the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) and Inertial Navigation System (INS) meets the positioning requirements of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) across a wide range of scenarios. However, these systems are not suitable for localization within GPS-denied environments. This paper proposes a tightly coupled fusion algorithm that integrates Ultra-Wideband (UWB) and Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) data based on Time Difference of Arrival (TDOA) measurements, suitable for using in GPS-denied environments. TDOA algorithm reduces communication burden, reduces power consumption and enhances positioning accuracy. Furthermore, the tightly coupled architecture enables the updating of UAV positioning information in harsh environments and enhances positioning accuracy and robustness. The algorithm was tested in a Gazebo-simulated UAV flight, comparing it against traditional and loosely coupled approaches, also using Two-Way Time of Flight (TW-TOF) measurements for internal comparisons. Results demonstrate that the method significantly enhances positioning accuracy and stability, achieving a median error of 0.0319 m, a 95 th percentile error of 0.0789 m, and an average standard deviation of 0.0207 m. This study validates the improvements in UWB positioning accuracy and robustness, promoting its application in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Robust adaptive collaborative navigation algorithm for UWB Non line of sight and Multipath in underground spaces
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Control (RAIIC)
abstract: This article addresses the Non Line of Sight (NLOS) and multipath issues in ultra wide band (UWB) range sensors for collaborative navigation of multiple unmanned vehicles in underground spaces. An anomaly detection algorithm Robust Random Cut Forest (RRCF) is used. Based on this, an improved robust adaptive Square Root Cubature Kalman filter (SRCKF) collaborative navigation algorithm based on Huber correction and Myers Tapley adaptation is proposed. Huber correction is used to correct outliers after RRCF detection, and Myers Tapley method adaptively processes continuous time-varying anomaly ranging errors caused by possible long-term non line of sight and multipath. Finally, This article compares the performance of the SRCKF algorithm, robust algorithm without RRCF detection, and robust algorithm with RRCF detection when there are outliers through simulation. The average positioning error of the SRCKF algorithm is 0.34 m, and the average positioning error of the RRCF Huber collaborative navigation algorithm is 0.30 m, which improves performance by 11.8% measured by the average positioning error. It also eliminates the abnormal error caused by ranging outliers, verifying the performance of the RRCF Huber algorithm. In addition, the performance of the RRCF Huber algorithm with and without Myers Tapley adaptation is compared when there is continuous anomalous ranging error. It is found that the RRCF Huber algorithm performs poorly in the presence of continuous anomalous ranging error, with RMSE value of 0.89 m, after adding Myers Tapley adaptation, the RMSE value reduces to 0.42 m, the algorithm’s positioning performance improved by 52.8% measured by RMSE values, verifying the performance of the Myers Tapley adaptation.

articleTitle: K-means++ Algorithm Based on Spark Platform in Large-scale Tourism Data Mining in Cloud Computing Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Control (RAIIC)
abstract: With the acceleration of global economic integration and the rapid growth of tourism data, the processing and analysis of tourism data are facing severe challenges. In order to manage and analyze massive data effectively, it must use effective data mining technology. In order to solve this problem, this project plans to build a set of K-means++ algorithm for big data based on cloud computing and Apache Spark platform, aiming at improving the efficiency of big data clustering analysis. Spark is chosen as the development platform because it has strong storage capacity and scalability, and can effectively handle massive data. On this basis, a clustering method based on Kmeans is proposed, and the initial value is optimized, thus shortening the convergence speed and improving the stability and accuracy of clustering results. The implementation method includes first preprocessing large-scale tourism data, such as data cleaning and feature selection, then applying an improved K-means++ algorithm for data clustering, and finally analyzing the clustering results to identify potential trends and consumer behavior patterns in the tourism market. As the maximum number of iterations increases, the average intra cluster distance gradually decreases from 10.5 to 9.8, indicating that the clustering effect is gradually improving, that is, data points are more tightly concentrated within their respective clusters. This study provides an effective big data analysis tool for the tourism industry, helping it better understand customer needs, optimize service supply, and promote the development of personalized tourism products.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Reinforcement Binding Robot for Building Machinery
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Control (RAIIC)
abstract: In response to the issue of high labor costs in the steel bar bundling process on building machines, a new type of steel bar bundling robot for building machines is proposed, which has strong load-bearing capacity, large working range, and is easy to install. Firstly, design a series parallel robot driven by ropes, establish a mathematical model of the structure using MATLAB, analyze the changes in rope length and working range, and verify the results; Finally, an adaptive sliding film control strategy is adopted to control the motion error of the modified mathematical model. The results show that this structure can meet the requirements of the steel bar binding process on the building machine.

Author Keywords: Cable driven series parallel hybrid robot

articleTitle: Research on Psychological Test based on Large Language Model
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Control (RAIIC)
abstract: Traditional questionnaire-based psychological tests have many drawbacks, such as the subjects’ inaccurate understanding of the questions, incomplete answers, disguised intentions, one-way communication, closed answers, etc. This paper proposes a psychological test system design scheme based on pre-trained large language model (LLM), which makes use of LLM’s ability to learn and understand natural language and generate output. Complete the psychological test with the subjects through natural language human-computer dialogue.Taking the Cattell 16 Personality Factors Test (16PF) as an example, a natural corpus for large model training of psychological test was researched and compiled, and the psychological test model of two factors in 16PF was developed. Through test comparison, the psychological test model is better than the traditional questionnaire test effect.

articleTitle: MixFEAN: Enhancing Multi-Object Tracking for Intelligent Sports Analysis through Conditional Feature Mixing and Dynamic Re-weighting
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Control (RAIIC)

abstract: Multi-object tracking (MOT) technology plays a key role in intelligent sports event analysis, and is essential for automating athlete data collection, assisting referee decision-making, and enhancing spectator experience. However, existing MOT systems often face challenges such as inconsistent detection accuracy and recognition difficulties, which stem from problems caused by the fast and complex context of the sport. To address these challenges, we propose an innovative approach called Mixed Feature Enhanced Attention Network (MixFEAN), which aims to improve the performance of multi-target tracking systems in complex scenarios through an integrated strategy of data enhancement and feature enhancement. Specifically, we introduce a feature-level conditional mixed data enhancement technique, FcMixup, which mixes the most similar feature representations during training to enhance the model’s adaptability to different motion behaviors and environmental changes. In addition, we design a novel Feature Decoupling Re-weighting Module (FDRM) that dynamically adjusts the weights of the feature maps so that the model is more focused on the identification and tracking of key targets, thus effectively improving the detection accuracy and enhancing the anti-jamming capability. The uniqueness of MixFEAN lies not only in the diversified data, but also in the optimization of the feature extraction through the noticing mechanism, thus enhancing the overall performance of the system while Maintaining Efficiency. We conducted extensive experiments on public datasets such as LSP and SportsMOT. The results show that MixFEAN improves the accuracy by $1.1 \%$ on the LSP dataset and significantly improves it on the SportsMOT dataset. These findings not only demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of the MixFEAN method in real-world scenarios, but also provide strong technical support for the further development of intelligent sports monitoring systems.
